mechanism: Isoniazid inhibits CYP2D6 and CYP3A4, increasing bupropion plasma concentrations and seizure risk; bupropion lowers seizure threshold while isoniazid can cause peripheral neuropathy and CNS effects.
action: Monitor closely for increased bupropion adverse effects including seizures, insomnia, and tremor; consider bupropion dose reduction if co-administered; ensure adequate pyridoxine supplementation with isoniazid to minimize neuropathy risk.
